text:
olivia (customer): Hey team — we have a production customer hitting repeated SSE stalls. Stream starts fine, emits ~10-15 events, then stops for ~30-90s, then reconnects and continues. Affected users are behind a corporate proxy. Happens in Chrome 114/115 desktop. No Safari reports. They say it started after we flipped the new CDN rule last week.

maya (support): sorry you're seeing this, olivia. Can you paste the full request/response headers from the browser/network tab and any relevant server logs? Also which CDN & edge rule did you flip?

olivia (customer): Here are snippets — browser shows the EventSource request to https://stream.example.com/live/abc123 with these request headers:

```
:method: GET
:authority: stream.example.com
:scheme: https
accept: text/event-stream
cache-control: no-cache
authorization: Bearer eyJ... (shortened)
user-agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7) Chrome/114.0.0
```

Response headers (first ~10s of stream):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
transfer-encoding: chunked
cache-control: no-cache, private
connection: keep-alive
etag: "v1-abc"

: then a few chunks of SSE data - events stream fine
```

After ~15 events we start seeing this in the network panel:
```
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
cache-control: public, max-age=60
age: 12
via: 1.1 corporate-proxy
x-edge-cache: HIT
```

That 304 coincides with the stream pause. Then after ~45s the client reconnects and gets a fresh 200 and events resume.

maya (support): interesting. So the client is getting a 304 mid-stream — that's unusual for SSE. Do you have any intermediate proxies or CDN that could be converting/short-circuiting the request? Which CDN rule did you flip?

olivia (customer): We enabled an edge ETag caching rule for GET resources (trying to reduce cost). The stream endpoint was accidentally included. We also use a corporate forward proxy for users that rewrites 302/307s and strips Authorization on redirects.

james (eng-runtime): thanks for the details — first pass: SSE must be treated as non-cacheable by intermediaries. If a CDN/edge issues a 304 in response to an If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since it effectively ends the chunked response from an origin perspective and the browser shows a pause while the edge serves a cached 304 body (which is empty). The EventSource connection expects an open chunked response; receiving a terminal 304 will stop the inflight stream until a reconnect.

A few probable contributors here:
- The edge rule allowed ETag/304 behavior for the SSE path (should be excluded).
- The corporate proxy is doing redirect handling (307) and may strip the Authorization header on a redirect or forward, causing the edge to serve a cached variant or trigger a conditional response.
- Some polyfills/fallbacks convert SSE to XHR long-polling and those responses are more cacheable. Do you know if users are on any SSE polyfill?

olivia (customer): they have a polyfill enabled for older IE fallback in their app bundle. But desktop Chrome should use native EventSource. The proxy path includes a transparent auth redirect to puppeteer auth endpoint that might cause a 307 at the edge.

maya (support): can you reproduce with curl from inside the corporate network or via a similar proxy? A simple test:

```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  "https://stream.example.com/live/abc123"
```

Look for any 3xx or 304 responses mid-stream.

olivia (customer): ran curl via the corp proxy — saw a 307 redirect then a 304. Here's truncated output:

```
> GET /live/abc123 HTTP/1.1
> Host: stream.example.com
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED

< HTTP/1.1 307 Temporary Redirect
< Location: https://edge.corp-auth/continue

# corp proxy follows redirect but drops Authorization header when forwarding
> GET /continue HTTP/1.1
> Host: edge.corp-auth
> Accept: text/event-stream

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< ETag: "v1-abc"
< Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
< Age: 0
< X-Edge-Cache: HIT

# after some time, edge returns 304
< HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
```

james (eng-runtime): that log nails it — redirect + header strip means the second request lacks auth and the edge may treat it as a different cache key or return a cached 304 variant. Two paths to break: the corporate proxy following redirects and removing Authorization, and the CDN treating SSE as cacheable.

Recommended short-term mitigations:
- Exclude /live/* SSE endpoints from the CDN ETag caching rule (set Cache-Control: no-store or no-cache and disable surrogate caching). Add a route exception.
- Ensure origin sets `Cache-Control: no-store, no-transform` and remove ETag for SSE responses. Avoid sending Last-Modified/ETag headers for event-stream endpoints.
- If possible, instruct the corporate proxy not to follow redirects for streaming endpoints (so the Authorization header is preserved).
- On the client: detect 304 as a stall and implement backoff/reconnect quicker (we can provide a small client-side probe).

olivia (customer): we can patch edge rules quickly. Any recommended header set exactly?

james (eng-runtime): here's a recommended minimal set for SSE responses from origin:
```
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0
Pragma: no-cache
Surrogate-Control: no-store
Connection: keep-alive
# omit ETag and Last-Modified entirely for SSE
```

And ensure the CDN edge respects the origin's Cache-Control and does not synthesize ETag/304 for that path. For CDN config examples (CloudFront/Akamai) set the behavior to "bypass cache" or treat as dynamic.

maya (support): also worth adding a guard on the server that rejects any upstream request that arrives without the Authorization header (so you fail fast) — but in this case we can't rely on that because proxy rewrites may be intentional.

olivia (customer): we flipped the edge rule and pushed the no-store headers. After the change the corp-reproduced curl shows continuous 200 chunked responses, no 304s. Can you confirm we should also remove ETag generation in our streaming framework?

james (eng-runtime): yes, remove ETag and any middleware that injects conditional cache validators on event-stream endpoints. Also add a monitoring rule in Console: alert if response status changes to 3xx/304 on an SSE route or if connection duration falls below X seconds. We can add a temporary trace filter for that customer.

replay-bot: Deploy 2026-03-12T08:41:02 completed for edge rule change (id: edge-rule-789).

edge-bot: Edge cache bypass enabled for /live/* — propagation 120s.

olivia (customer): Verified in-prod with a user behind the corporate proxy — stream no longer stalls. Thanks! :tada:

maya (support): great — marking this as resolved for now. Follow-ups:
- james: can we add a defensive check on the runtime that logs if a streaming response includes ETag/Last-Modified and raise an internal warning?
- olivia: if you see any other oddities with other proxies, please reopen.

james (eng-runtime): will add a lint in the streaming middleware and an alert rule. Also adding a note in docs: "Never enable origin/CDN caching for text/event-stream — use no-store/no-transform."

olivia (customer): thanks all!"
